rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 9 chunks. Chunk 0 line 9 ("Come to Module 1 with the repo picked, the curated skills installed, and one trivial bug") reads like a forward pointer to Steps 1/4/5, but it is a generic topic-sentence preview (definite article used generically, like a deck's own thesis line), not a broken pointer requiring the reader to already hold an antecedent — the harm rule 1 guards against (losing track of what a pronoun points to) is absent since nothing downstream depends on resolving it before it's elaborated. Chunk 3 "that repo" correctly resolves to chunk 2's just-picked repo (sequential, in-file). No never-named or vague-with-history referents found.
Chunk 2 line 36 names "Build a project from zero" by title (carve-out: navigational pointer, named not located). No file pointed at by position ("the opening lecture said").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No "the X you did/saw" backward beat references anywhere in the file — this is the training's first artefact, nothing prior exists to point at.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal demo beat in this file.
Every chunk carries a self-contained claim or instruction; none is a bare wait-state bullet.

Checked all 9 headers against their chunk content (What to bring / Pick THE repo / Open a Claude Code session / Get the content folder / Extract the bundle and install skills / Pick a trivial bug and confirm readiness / Pre-read before Module 1 / Bring to Module 1) — each accurately summarizes its chunk; none is contradicted by its own body.

Checked all sub-items across all chunks: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative (no value-prop leak); no number-with-retraction ("30 to 120 minutes" stands unretracted); no abstraction-noun stacks; no empty-leg verb triplets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scanned for surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun — none present. "Session" is used as ordinary Claude Code terminology (a Claude Code session), not repo-internal dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "What to bring" line 22: "**Separate tasks off your backlog.**" bolds a full standalone imperative sentence, not a ≲5-word handle — the rule bans this shape explicitly ("never a whole lead sentence") independent of whether the list above it qualifies for the menu carve-out, because the carve-out lifts only the ≤1-per-slide count, not the handle-vs-sentence distinction. Harm: a bolded full sentence competes visually with the four genuine item-handles above it (Trivial bug / A small multi-file task / A small feature / A bigger piece), diluting exactly the scan signal rule 9 exists to protect — present here, not just a shape match. || chunk 7 "Pre-read before Module 1" line 117: "**Read: Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Oct/7/vibe-engineering/)**" bolds mode-word plus author plus title together. This chunk is a reading-list slide, so the ≤1-per-slide count is waived by rule 9's own carve-out, but that carve-out's worked example is this exact shape: "bold the mode word alone (**Read:**...) and leave the title plain. Bolding mode-plus-title is the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture wearing a list for cover." Harm present: the reader can no longer find the mode word (Read/Watch) at a glance because the whole line reads as one undifferentiated bold block.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Chunk 1: drop the bold on "Separate tasks off your backlog.", make it plain trailing prose. Chunk 7: bold only "Read:" and leave "Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering](...)" unbolded.
